Question 5: If the first and the third letters of each word are interchanged, and the new words thus formed are arranged in alphabetical order from left to right, how many of the original words will retain their original position in the sequence?
records.explanation: The original sequence and positions are: RED(1) OFF(2) SUM(3) HAG(4) JIB(5) First, interchange the first and third letters of each word: RED -> DER OFF -> FFO SUM -> MUS HAG -> GAH JIB -> BIJ The new set of words is: DER, FFO, MUS, GAH, BIJ. Next, arrange these new words in alphabetical order: BIJ, DER, FFO, GAH, MUS Now, trace back to the original words that formed these new words: BIJ came from JIB. DER came from RED. FFO came from OFF. GAH came from HAG. MUS came from SUM. So, the new order of the original words is: JIB(1) RED(2) OFF(3) HAG(4) SUM(5) Finally, compare this new order with the original order: Original: RED(1) OFF(2) SUM(3) HAG(4) JIB(5) New: JIB(1) RED(2) OFF(3) HAG(4) SUM(5) The word 'HAG' is at position 4 in both the original and the new sequence. Therefore, only one word retains its original position.
